rounds.text: Loyal Textile Mills is currently undergoing a significant financial restructuring that is not yet reflected in its market valuation. The company has aggressively reduced its debt from Rs 413 Cr to Rs 216 Cr in the last year [E35, E51], which directly improves its long-term solvency profile. This deleveraging coincides with a powerful operational turnaround, evidenced by a 70% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E17] and a notable improvement in quarterly operating margins from -11% to -3% [E27]. The stock is currently trading at a deep discount of 0.51x book value [E1, E52], suggesting that the market has yet to price in the company's ability to generate substantial cash, as seen in the Rs 229 Cr of free cash flow reported in March 2026 [E32]. Furthermore, the technical setup shows the stock trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, indicating a shift in momentum [E42]. Conceded: the company faces significant headwinds including a -38% decline in trailing twelve-month sales [E16], a negative return on equity [E12], and a tight liquidity position with a current ratio of 0.85x [E34].

Conceded: [E31], [E32], [E35], [E42], [E52]. Despite these isolated positive markers, Loyal Textile Mills Ltd carries severe structural and fundamental risks that are not supported by healthy underlying business performance. Compounded sales growth has cratered across every measured timeframe, declining by 10% over 10 years, 18% over 5 years, 33% over 3 years, and plunging 38% in the trailing twelve months [E13, E14, E15, E16]. Profitability metrics are deeply negative, highlighted by a trailing ROE of -25.8% and a median ROE of -25% over the last 3 years, severely lagging sector benchmarks [E8, E12, E24]. Balance sheet and solvency pressures remain acute, evidenced by a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.06x where debt exceeds net worth, a low current ratio of 0.85x, and a low interest coverage ratio [E33, E34, E53]. Furthermore, the stock exhibits extreme volatility of 53.1% alongside a poor Sharpe ratio of -0.43 and a devastating historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -82.1% [E46, E47, E45].

Conceded: [E13], [E14], [E15], [E16], [E8], [E12], [E24], [E46], [E47], [E45]. While those historical growth and volatility metrics look grim, the bear overlooks a fundamental corporate restructuring that changes the forward trajectory: borrowings dropped dramatically from Rs 413 Cr to Rs 216 Cr within a single year [E35], directly validating management's debt reduction strategy [E51]. This aggressive balance sheet cleanup has already unlocked massive cash generation, delivering an extraordinary free cash flow of Rs 229 Cr alongside operating cash flow of Rs 89 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32]. Furthermore, the business is in the middle of a sharp operational turnaround that stale sentiment ignores [E64], evidenced by quarterly operating margins surging by 8 percentage points to -3% in June 2026 compared to -11% in the year-ago quarter [E27]. Profit growth has exploded by 70% over the trailing twelve months with recent quarterly net profit up 91% YoY [E17, E58], significantly outpacing 1-year price growth and signaling that expectations are being beaten [E49]. Trading at a deeply discounted price-to-book ratio of just 0.51x [E1], the stock is firmly above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with positive technical momentum [E42], confirming that the market is beginning to reprice this improving cash-rich asset.

Conceded: [E35]. While borrowings dropped from Rs 413 Cr to Rs 216 Cr [E35], the debt-to-equity ratio remains burdened at 1.06x where debt still exceeds net worth [E33], alongside a weak current ratio of 0.85x indicating current liabilities exceed current assets [E34]. The claim of an operational turnaround is contradicted by an inconsistent yearly operating margin trend [E28] and an inconsistent quarterly trend [E29], with the TTM operating margin remaining deeply negative at -4% [E26]. Although the bull cites high free cash flow of Rs 229 Cr [E32], the company reported a loss year in March 2026 where the cash conversion ratio of -1.37x is not meaningful due to those losses [E30], and earnings are artificially padded by other income of Rs 7.75 Cr [E56]. Furthermore, compounded sales growth continues to deteriorate severely, falling by -38% over the trailing twelve months [E16] and -33% over three years [E15]. Finally, despite technical momentum [E42], the stock carries an exceptionally high annualised volatility of 53.1% [E46] and a negative Sharpe ratio of -0.43 [E47], while long-term share price growth remains negative across 1, 3, 5, and 10-year horizons [E18, E19, E20, E21].
